notes: Page 2 shows only the assembly of the Emma mini-doll figure (hair, head, torso, legs). The doll parts are not in the parts list or the catalogue, so nothing is recorded. The page also has a choking-hazard warning and no brick-building step.

Step 1: the reddish-brown round plate goes on the lime round brick. Step 2: the bamboo-leaf plant goes in the centre of the brown plate. Step 3: the orange flower goes on top of the plant's central stud. The catalogue lists only an anti-stud for lego-30176, but the real part has a top stud, so I recorded the flower as resting on it.

Step 1: a pink 2x2 brick goes on one end of a white 2x4 plate. Step 2: a white 2x6 plate extends the base, so the base grows longer. The drawings are small and I could not tell exactly how the plates overlap. I recorded the 2x6 plate as resting on the 2x4 plate only; its true overlap with the 2x4 plate and the pink brick is a guess. The small inset at the top left shows this is the start of the sun-lounger with a green parasol.

Step 3: lime round 1x1 plates are pressed onto the underside of the white plate to act as feet. Step 4 shows two feet, so I recorded two; the first is already visible under the plate in the step 3 drawing. Step 4: a white sloped brick goes at the high end of the 2x6 plate. Four 1x2 tiles follow in the order lime, pink, lime, pink, each across the plate. The pink 2x2 brick stays at the back. The feet attach to the 2x6 plate b7, which is a guess; the drawings are small.

Step 5: a white round 1x1 open-stud brick goes on the pink 2x2 brick. The white 6L bar is pushed down into its open stud as the parasol pole. The bar has no stud and clutches nothing below, so rests_on is empty and the join is in other_joins.

The inset builds a drink: an orange flower goes on the clear goblet (inset step 1), then a pink round plate goes on the flower (inset step 2). Step 6 places the finished drink on the pink 2x2 brick, beside the parasol pole. The goblet has no ports in the catalogue; I recorded it as standing on a free stud of b6, and the same for the flower on the goblet.

Step 7: an orange flower goes on the centre stud of the inverted lime dish (the parasol top). The dish then goes on top of the white bar b16. The dish's underside clutches the bar's top end, so I recorded it as resting on b16.

This page starts a new sub-assembly, the pool, shown in the top-left inset. Step 1: two pink round-corner 3x3 plates are placed side by side along their straight edges. Step 2: a trans-light-blue 1x2x1 panel is placed on the left plate near the back edge. I recorded it on b22 only, because it looks to sit on one plate, not across the seam. The two plates have no direct stud connection; the other_joins entry is only a note that they touch.

Step 3: two more trans-light-blue panels go on the left and right sides of the pink floor. A Medium Azure macaroni corner brick goes on the back. Step 4: the last two pink round-corner plates extend the floor towards the front, so the pink base becomes a rounder oval. The drawings are small, so which plates the new pieces clutch is a best guess. The two new floor plates are recorded only as touching their neighbours, since I could not tell if anything holds them to the pieces beneath. The azure brick is recorded as spanning both floor plates and the first panel.

Step 5: a pink 2x2 tile goes in the middle of the floor, over the four pink plates. A white 2x2 plate is attached at the front edge as the start of the entry steps. Step 6: a second white 2x2 plate is added in line with it, making a longer step. The drawings are small, so which pieces the white plate clutches is a best guess. The white 2x2 plate b31 is shown slightly below the floor, so I joined it up into the front pink plates, not resting it on them. The tile covers a 2x2 area over the centre seam, so I listed all four floor plates under it.

Step 7: a white 1x2 plate goes on the white 2x2 step plate nearest the pool. Step 8: the pool rim is finished by three more Medium Azure macaroni corner bricks, which with b27 make four around the edge. The lime step surfaces in the drawing do not match the parts-list count exactly. I recorded one lime 1x2 tile on the outer step plate b32, and the remaining lime and pink tiles are left for later pages. Which pieces each rim brick clutches is a best guess from small drawings.

This page shows the finished scene and has no building step: the pool, the lounger with parasol and drink, the flower pot and the Emma mini-doll. No pieces were added. The parts list says 2 pink 1x2 tiles are still unplaced. They are probably the two pink stripes of the lounger (b12, b14) or the pool steps. The earlier pages' lime and pink tile counts do not fully match the parts list, so I may have mis-coloured some tiles. I did not change earlier entries.
Advertising page for other LEGO Friends sets (3183, 3061, 3065, 3187, 3942, 3936, 3188, 3934, 3315). There is no building step, so nothing is added.

Back cover with a survey competition advertisement and legal text. There is no building step, so nothing is added. The 2 pink 1x2 tiles from the parts list were never clearly shown as placed on any page. They are probably the two pink stripes already recorded on the lounger (b12, b14), where the earlier tile counts did not match the parts list.

This is not a real problem, so I added nothing. The booklet builds three separate models: (1) the flower pot (b1-b4, page 3), (2) the sun-lounger with parasol and drink (b5-b21, pages 4-8) and (3) the pool with its entry steps (b22-b37, pages 9-12). Page 13 shows them standing apart in the scene with the Emma mini-doll, and no step joins one model to another. Joining them would invent connections the booklet does not show. The mini-doll is not in the parts list or catalogue, so it is not recorded. The 2 pink 1x2 tiles left over in the parts list are most likely the lounger's two pink stripes (b12, b14). I could not match them exactly, so earlier entries are unchanged.

This is the same warning again and it is still not a real problem, so I added nothing. Set 3931-1 really builds three separate models: the flower pot (b1-b4), the sun-lounger with parasol and drink (b5-b21) and the pool with entry steps (b22-b37). Page 13 shows them standing apart in the scene, and no booklet step attaches one to another. Any joins between them would be made up. Each group is internally connected, and the three groups are meant to stay separate.
